Theme

Nature & food

flood noun and verb

also floods, flooding, flooded, be flooded, the Flood, deluge, overflow

classical

Suet. Oth. 8: inundātiōnēs Tiberis (Lewis & Short)
Col. 3.11.8: flūminum

inundātiō, inundātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a flood, the overflowing of a river

(post-Augustan prose: Col., Suet., Plin.)

The water spreading over the land; the verb is inundō, classical in Cicero and Livy, of a river or rain flooding the fields, and also, without an object, of the river overflowing (Arnus inundāverat, Liv. 22.2.2).

Other words

  • dīluvium, dīluviī n. — a flood, a deluge; the Flood

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 8.17.1: crēbra dīluvia; Sen. Q.N. 3.27 (the great flood, Lewis & Short)

    (vōx poētica et post-Augustēa: Verg., Ov.; Sen., Plin. Ep.)

    Also dīluviēs (Lucr., Hor.). In Seneca and in Christian Latin the Flood (dīluvium, Vulg. Matt. 24.38).

  • ēluviō, ēluviōnis f. — a flood, an inundation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.111: aquārum ēluviōnēs (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s word, beside exustiō, for the floods and burnings of the earth.

Examples

  • Tiberis agrōs inundāvit

    the Tiber flooded the fieldsLiv. 24.9 (Lewis & Short)

  • num istīc quoque immīte et turbidum caelum? hīc assiduae tempestātēs et crēbra dīluvia

    is the sky wild and stormy there too? here it is storm after storm and flood after floodPlin. Ep. 8.17.1

See also rain, river, storm, weather.
